acceptance_criteria.criterion: MaxLengthValidation class exists in Validation/Type/, extends BaseParamValidation, and its validate() method produces an error with code VALIDATION_MAX_LENGTH_EXCEEDED when a non-empty string value exceeds the configured $maxLength (measured with mb_strlen()).
MaxLengthValidation::validate() returns without error for null, empty string (''), and non-string values.
ParamValidationInterface contains a new VALIDATION_MAX_LENGTH_EXCEEDED constant following the existing integer numbering series.
StringParameter::setMaxLength(int $maxLength) exists, registers a MaxLengthValidation instance, returns $this, and is usable in fluent chains.

MaxLengthValidationTest covers at minimum: exact boundary (value length == maxLength passes), over boundary (value length > maxLength fails), null skip, empty-string skip, and integration with StringParameter::setMaxLength().

comments.note: MaxLengthValidation calls mb_strlen() twice when a value exceeds the limit (once for the check, once for the error message). Storing the result in a local variable would eliminate the redundant call. Trivial but worth noting.

StringParameter.php already had a validateByRegex() helper wrapping validateBy(). The new setMaxLength() follows the same naming convention for direct validators, but the two helpers use different naming conventions (setMaxLength vs validateByRegex). Future helpers should settle on one pattern (either 'validateBy*' or 'set*') to keep the API consistent.

BaseParamValidation is currently an abstract class with no abstract methods or shared logic — it exists only as a type anchor. If more validators are added, consider whether a small shared utility (e.g., isValidatable(mixed $value): bool) would reduce boilerplate across the Type/ validators.

summary: Full API test suite (408 tests, 934 assertions) is green — no regressions. Warnings and PHPUnit notices are pre-existing in OpenAPI tests, unrelated to this WP.

All 6 acceptance criteria verified: MaxLengthValidation extends BaseParamValidation, uses mb_strlen(), skips null/empty/non-string, emits VALIDATION_MAX_LENGTH_EXCEEDED (183507), setMaxLength() on StringParameter returns $this and integrates correctly.
Edge-case stress: maxLength=0 correctly rejects any non-empty string; boolean true/false are safely skipped by the !is_string() guard.

comments.note: maxLength=0 correctly rejects any non-empty string (mb_strlen('a') > 0 is true). No special-case guard needed — the existing logic handles it cleanly.

Boolean true/false values (passed as non-string) are safely skipped by the !is_string() guard in validate(). The test suite covers integer non-string skipping; booleans are equally protected by the same branch.

Pre-existing PHPUnit notices (67) and warnings (2) in the OpenAPI test suite are unrelated to this WP — confirmed by isolating the MaxLengthValidation and Parameters test subsets which produce zero notices/warnings.

summary: [PASS with Fix-Forward] Code quality is solid. Architecture follows established patterns correctly. One trivial non-behavioral fix applied directly (mb_strlen double-call). Two documentation-forward items tagged for the Documentation agent. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: MaxLengthValidation::validate() — eliminated redundant mb_strlen() call. Extracted result into local variable $length before the conditional, then reused $length inside sprintf(). Non-behavioral: no logic or output change, QA validation remains fully intact.

[documentation-forward] StringParameter exposes two naming conventions for validator-registering helpers: validateByRegex() (procedural, validateBy* prefix) and setMaxLength() (property-setter style, set* prefix). The class docblock should document which convention is preferred for future additions, or acknowledge that both styles coexist and why.

[documentation-forward] BaseParamValidation is an empty abstract class used purely as a type anchor. Its class-level docblock should explain this design intent explicitly — e.g., 'Serves as a concrete base type for all parameter validators; no shared logic is provided here intentionally. Future shared utilities (e.g. isValidatable()) should be added here rather than duplicated across Type/ validators.'

StringParameter::getValue() calls parent::getValue() twice when the value is a string (lines 145–148). This is pre-existing and outside this WP scope, but worth a future cleanup: store parent::getValue() in a local variable and return it directly.
